text: Affordance: every clickable control MUST look clickable, and an element that cannot be clicked MUST NOT look clickable.
checklist: Each affordance finding quotes a control whose look and behaviour disagree.

text: Feedback: every action MUST be followed by a visible response; an action longer than 1 second MUST show a loading or progress state; a completed save, send, payment or delete MUST be confirmed on screen.
checklist: Each feedback finding quotes an action whose handler or next step shows no response, loading state or confirmation.

text: System status: the screen MUST show the current step and the number of steps in a flow of 3 or more steps, what is selected, which filter or mode is on, and whether changes are saved.
checklist: Each status finding names the state that is not visible.

text: Mapping: every control MUST sit inside or next to the thing it changes, and a set of controls MUST follow the same order as the things they control.
checklist: Each mapping finding names the control and the thing it changes.

text: Error prevention: an action that deletes, pays, sends or overwrites MUST have a confirmation step or an undo; a field with a required format or limit MUST state it before the user submits.
checklist: Each prevention finding quotes the destructive action or the field.

text: Error recovery: an error message MUST appear next to its cause, MUST say what to do next, and the screen MUST keep everything the user entered.
checklist: Each recovery finding quotes the error path.

text: Choices: one step MUST offer at most 7 choices at one level; a longer list MUST have groups, a search or a preselected default.
checklist: Each choice finding gives the count of choices.

text: Reach: a control the main goal needs MUST be easy enough to hit that the user does not miss it or hit its neighbour; a hit problem is a finding about what the user does wrong, never a measurement, and its recommendation ends with "; the sizes are for ui-polish."
checklist: Each reach finding says what the user does wrong, quotes the size only as evidence, states no px threshold and names ui-polish.

text: Grouping: targets used one after the other in the same step MUST be in the same visible group, and neighbouring targets with opposite effects MUST be visibly separated; the review states no pixel gap, and when the cause is a gap or a size the recommendation ends with "; the sizes are for ui-polish."
checklist: Each grouping finding names the two groups or the two opposite controls and states no px gap and, when the cause is a gap or size, names ui-polish.

text: Memory load: the user MUST have 0 things to remember between steps; every value needed later is shown where it is needed, and nothing already entered is asked again.
checklist: Each memory finding names the value and the two steps.

text: Consistency: the same action MUST have the same label and position on every screen of the input, and one label MUST NOT name two different actions.
checklist: Each consistency finding quotes both labels or positions.

text: Familiar patterns: a control MUST behave as its row in the familiar-pattern table says.
checklist: Each pattern finding matches a row P1 to P7 of the table.

text: Steps: the main goal MUST be reachable in at most 5 steps, and every step MUST collect or show something the main goal needs.
checklist: The step count is stated and each steps finding names the step.

text: Every finding MUST quote evidence that is present in the input; what the input does not show MUST go under Open questions and is NEVER guessed.
checklist: Each evidence quote appears in the input, and no finding rests on something not shown.

text: Every finding MUST carry exactly one severity: S1 Blocker, S2 Major, S3 Minor or S4 Note, chosen with the ordered questions.
checklist: Each finding has one severity and it follows the ordered questions.

text: Every finding MUST have exactly one recommendation, one sentence in words; NEVER code, replacement wording or a new layout.
checklist: Each recommendation is one sentence with no code and no replacement wording.

text: NEVER fix, rewrite or produce code; a request to fix the code MUST get the exact sentence "This skill reviews usability; it does not change code. To fix the code, use ui-polish.".
checklist: The reply has no code block, and a fix request starts with the exact sentence.

text: NEVER report contrast ratios, focus styles, spacing or type scales, semantics, ARIA or screen-reader output, and NEVER rewrite text; a request for one MUST get its exact sentence.
checklist: The reply reports none of these and gives the exact sentence when one was asked for.

text: With no screen or flow in the message, the reply MUST be exactly "Paste the screen's code or describe the flow step by step." and nothing else.
checklist: With nothing to review, the reply is only the exact sentence.

text: A request to design a new screen MUST get the exact sentence "This skill reviews an existing screen or flow; it does not design new screens. To design a screen, use ui-craft." and no design.
checklist: A design request gets the exact sentence and no design.

text: The reply MUST follow the output format; findings are numbered 1 to N, most severe first, one place and one rule per finding.
checklist: The reply has every section in order, numbers 1 to N, and severities that never rise down the list.

text: The skill MUST have the ten core layers, each linked from SKILL.md.
The skill MUST be self-contained; NEVER name a repository path in SKILL.md, layers or references.
SKILL.md MUST stay within 150 lines, with frontmatter name, description and semver version.
Every relative link MUST point to a file inside the skill folder.

First screen: the first screen (1440 by 900 px or 390 by 844 px unless the layout input says otherwise) MUST say in words what the product or screen is and who it is for, and the first element seen MUST be that heading or its sentence; a cover, picture or sample output MUST NOT push the heading below the first screen.
checklist: Each first-screen finding quotes the first element seen or the heading position from the layout input, or the first heading in the code.

text: Section order: sections MUST follow the order of the user's task (what it is, proof, the main action, then details); the section with the main action MUST start within the first 3 screens; a lead-in sentence MUST NOT sit above the heading it introduces.
checklist: Each order finding names the two sections and quotes their tops or their order in the code.

text: Page length: a page MUST be at most 6 screens tall and no section taller than 2 screens, unless the extra part sits behind a control that opens it.
checklist: Each length finding gives the page height or section height in px and in screens.

text: Duplicated blocks: the same content (the same text of 20 words or more, the same answer, list or picture) MUST NOT be shown twice on one page unless the second is a short link to the first.
checklist: Each duplicate finding quotes the content and names both places.

text: Calls to action: a view MUST hold at most 1 primary action, and the first screen at most 7 controls that compete in its content (hero actions, cards); persistent navigation (a header, rail or sidebar that repeats on every screen) is counted apart, judged by R-ux-review-7, and never added to that count; a primary action repeated on every card of a list counts once per card in view.
checklist: Each call-to-action finding gives the content count and the persistent-navigation count apart and names the view.

text: A break that depends on a script, handler, data or run-time content that the input refers to but does not contain (this includes text and state the missing script could set or replace) MUST NOT be S1 or S2; it is S3 at most, with an open question naming the missing script, or only an open question.
checklist: No S1 or S2 finding rests on a script that is not in the input.

text: Pages built from one template MUST give one finding for a break that comes from the template, naming the template and listing the pages; a break on one page is its own finding.
checklist: A template break appears once and lists its pages.

text: NEVER report a design token's name, value or absence as a finding, and never review tokens (design-system) or contrast (a11y-audit); a token is only resolved to a number as evidence for a finding about the task.
checklist: No finding is about a token; a token appears only inside an evidence quote.
